findings.statement: The exact Chromium 151 source uses adjacent-bucket randomized rounding at 100 us for non-isolated contexts. Each endpoint error is bounded approximately by one bucket; two endpoints can differ by almost two buckets. The common clamped time origin cancels. The clamp-only duration envelope is about plus/minus 200 us, with a separately derived small conversion/floating allowance, not the 100 us observed minimum step.
findings.status: Source-derived feasibility bound, not yet an admitted runtime/binary-bound protocol.

findings.statement: The pinned WebKit upstream uses default 1 ms floor rounding; for fixed precision each timestamp error lies between minus one bucket and zero, so a whole duration has error less than plus/minus 1 ms, plus a conservative numeric allowance. Playwright's complete exact bootstrap patch contains none of the identified precision-code changes.
findings.status: Source-derived bound for the declared bundled Linux WebKit lineage, not a claim about iPhone Safari.

findings.statement: Current application work sampling starts once at Phaser PRE_STEP and ends once at POST_RENDER. It is one whole-work interval. A sum of separate measured intervals instead needs endpoint-count accounting unless shared endpoint terms cancel algebraically.

Current workflow installs pinned Playwright and bundled browsers, but timer collection permits CHROME_EXECUTABLE and retains observed versions without enforcing the exact expected version value. Existing observed minimum-step calibration alone does not establish a duration-error upper bound. Source lineage, actual executable path/version/provenance, flags, non-isolation, precision branch and unchanged instrumentation must be bound automatically before a future source-derived envelope can qualify.

Use matched run-level p95 values as the paired observations, not individual frames as independent replicates. Existing paired log-ratio interval assumes sufficiently independent pairs and suitable paired-log-ratio behavior; preserve order/host/drift data and examine sensitivity. It estimates a geometric mean of run-p95 ratios, not a pooled-frame p95.

A newly reviewed, independently bound implementation envelope can preserve the original 5% target and existing per-frame p95 estimand. Qualification is possible only when the correctly widened upper ratio interval is at most 1.05; otherwise unresolved. More runs can reduce sampling uncertainty but cannot remove worst-case bounded quantization ambiguity.

This is a scoped engineering claim about declared browser binaries and recorded test conditions, not universal clock correctness or device equivalence. A plain empirical matched estimate remains useful evidence if its resolution, assumptions and sensitivity are explicit; it must not be silently promoted to the existing qualification gate using an unsupported bound.

Whole-block totals, repeating work many times, CPU throttling, high-resolution isolation changes or profiler-only traces cannot silently substitute for ordinary per-frame p95. They change the estimand, execution conditions or observer cost. A redesigned protocol needs explicit review against the same target.

Retain the original matched workload, 5% target, complete pair set and failure outcomes. Check order effects, per-run distributions, source identity, timer diagnostics and quantization sensitivity; do not choose a favorable subset.
Run only the explicitly admitted final-source cohort. Report measured estimate and interval separately from qualification; use unresolved when resolution or run-level variability prevents deciding.

If the declared coarse WebKit clock cannot resolve the target, design a separate matched measurement method and quantify observer effects before any qualification claim; do not reinterpret block averages as frame-p95.
